title: Convoy No. 3905, 9 September 1944
eyebrow: South of Honshu and east of Formosa · BANG's third war patrol

paras.text: BANG's attacks on convoy No. 3905, bound from Yokosuka for Haha-jima, as typed on her attack sheets, with her depth log and the Yokosuka Guard Squadron's diary of the same afternoon.

Tokiwasan Maru (1,804 tons) and Shoryu Maru (1,916 tons) sunk. The Yokosuka Guard Squadron's diary records both "torpedoed and sunk" at 1520 Tokyo time on the 9th, four minutes after BANG's first salvo (jacar:C08030363600 p3), but gives the place as 265° 10 nm from Sumisu-jima, about 188 nm north-east of BANG's attack; BANG's position agrees with the postwar one, 28-58N 137-45E (combinedfleet.com). BANG claimed a medium AK and a medium AO.
Yokosuka to Haha-jima (secondary). BANG saw 1 AO, 2 AK and 2 escorts. The convoy's own record: [[convoy:no-3905]].

Positions are BANG's own dead reckoning and star sights; lines between them are straight, and where she went in between is not recorded. Open circles are ships she sighted, at the target's position. As the clock passes each firing time a red ring pulses at BANG's position; hover a diamond for the attack sheet.
BANG kept zone K (−10) throughout. Japanese records use Tokyo time (I, −9).

Neither Japanese record for this patrol gives a time: combinedfleet.com's account of convoy No. 3905 and the 4th Surface Escort Division's daily summary for TAKA-909. Each is drawn at the time of the attack it matches, and marked so. FRUPAC's intercept has No. 3905's ships "torp & sunk 1520/09" (1520 I = 1620 K, between Attacks 1 and 2).

No Japanese record has been found yet for Attacks 5 and 6 (20–21 September); the 4th Escort diary has no attack on those days. Where the Japanese record names only the ships that were hit, the rest of the convoy is described as BANG saw it.

BANG's third war patrol report, NARA microfilm M1752 (74802831). The 4th Surface Escort Division / Okinawa Base Force war diary, September 1944, via JACAR (C08030144100, National Institute for Defense Studies). Convoy No. 3905 from combinedfleet.com, a secondary source, flagged where used. Coastline: Natural Earth.

bang.note: Departed Midway enroute area. Crossed date line (port position)

bang.words: Submerged as the bearing has remained constant ... I wanted to avoid possible plane detection.
Surfaced. Target had tracked as making two zigs to his left
Submerged. ... Commenced approach. ... Sea calm visibility excellent.
Rigged for silent running and dropped down to 75 feet keeping one sound head on target to TDC (time not stated; before 1616 firing)
Swung with escort until the firing course was reached then steadied came up to periscope depth
I swung around and saw that the leading escort was heading toward me - ordered 400 feet.
Received the first pattern of depth charges while passing 350 feet all above.
Running at 450 feet at 2/3 speed under a 17° negative gradient. ... During the next hour and a half they dropped about 70 depth charges many of them very close.
16 depth charges about one second apart above very slightly and to port very slightly. We were at 475 feet when they started (time approximate: ~1h50m after firing)

but the bow was knocked down and we were at 580 feet making standard speed with a 10 degree up angle before we caught the boat. ... I heard a definite thump on the hull followed by a tremendous explosion. I believe this was a depth charge that bounced off our side.
Surfaced. All clear. We found that the glass in the bridge gyro repeater was shattered the forward end of the periscope shears dented in

paras.text: The Japanese record of the loss is the Yokosuka Guard Squadron's September diary (p3): 昌隆丸 (Shoryu Maru) and 常盤山丸 (Tokiwasan Maru) torpedoed and sunk at 1520 on the 9th, four minutes after BANG's first salvo (1616 K = 1516 I). It gives the place as 265° 10 nm from Sumisu-jima, which is about 188 nm north-east of BANG's attack position; BANG's position agrees with the postwar one combinedfleet gives (28-58N 137-45E). The diary doesn't name the convoy.

The route and escorts are combinedfleet.com's (secondary). It has the convoy leave Yokosuka on 6 September for Haha-jima, reach Tateyama on the 7th, and leave Tateyama "at 1520" on the 9th, then be attacked "at about 1600" at 28-58N 137-45E. That can't be right: Tateyama is about 360 nm north of that position, and 1520 on the 9th is the diary's time of the sinking. The Tateyama sailing was probably the 7th or 8th (inferred, to check). The escort grid (p5) fits Yasojima (父島 across about days 8–11) but has CD-4 at Yokosuka and Tateyama until about the 10th; all read with low confidence from a skewed scan.
**Cargo: not recorded.** BANG saw one oiler (AO) and two freighters.

words.type_attack: Day periscope. Sound tracking for 12 minutes prior to firing to avoid detection by escort passing close aboard. Final periscope set-up to TDC just before firing, and constant bearing given during firing. Fired three torpedoes spread 1½, 0, 1½ from aft forward by means of the offset knob on the TDC.
words.description: Convoy consisted of one AO (nearest estimate, HOKKO MARU, ONI 208J (revised) page 265); one AK (nearest estimate, MYOGI or HOKUYO MARU, ONI 208J (revised) page 208); one unidentified medium AK; one new type destroyer escort; and one unidentified escort. Fired at leading AK. Clear daylight.
words.sunk: One AK (similar to MYOGI or HOKUYO MARU). EU.
words.determined_by: Saw and heard two hits, saw ship break in half. Heard breaking up noises through hull.
words.target_line: Target Draft: 24 Feet Course: 180° Speed: 10.0 Range: 1700 yds.
words.remarks: The miss was due to spread used.
words.note: Two specks after "245°" in the own-ship course line are marks on the paper, not typed characters (zoomed); the course is 245, and the tracks typed agree with 245 + gyro against target course 180.

words.type_attack: Immediately after firing in attack No. 1, gave new periscope set-up on AO to TDC, and constant bearings during firing. Fired three torpedoes spread 1½, 0, 1½ from aft forward by means of the offset knob on the TDC.
words.description: Same convoy as Attack No. 1. Fired at AO.
words.sunk: One AO (similar to HOKKO MARU). EU.
words.determined_by: Saw and heard two hits. Saw ship settling completely enveloped in dense smoke. Heard breaking up noises through hull.
words.target_line: Target Draft: 24 feet Course: 180° Speed: 10.0 Range: 1900 yds.
words.remarks: The miss was due to spread used.
words.note: The sheet's time is typed "1616-32(K)", and the narrative (rg38-74802831/p04) has "At 1616-32 Commenced firing three torpedoes at AO" straight after firing at the AK at 1616: 32 seconds after 1616. positions.csv has the minute, 1616 (it had 1632 until 31 Oct 2026, the seconds read as minutes); attacks.csv keeps 1616-32.
